notes: Both evaluate transcriptional bursting observations (C40, C41, C77, C78). LLM finds evidence convincing with quantified on/off durations and HMM analysis. Peer reviewers question missing baseline controls (0 μM PA) and whether dose-independence was confirmed across all clonal lines, indicating insufficient validation.

Both assess caged PA characterization (C62-C65). LLM finds chemical synthesis, purity, and antagonist properties well-documented. Peer reviewers question the mechanistic explanation, asking whether transient activation is truly due to excess caged PA blocking released PA, requesting proof of this presumed mechanism.

Both evaluate clonal variation and chromatin context effects (C57, C58, C82, C84). LLM finds evidence that insertion site affects transcription rate but not frequency modulation convincing. Peer reviewers question whether dose-dependent/independent parameters were validated for each clone individually, noting unclear data presentation in Figure 2.

Both express uncertainty about photoactivation results and the ~2 hour delay (C28, C67, C74, C90, C91). LLM notes 40% success rate and unexplained variability. Peer reviewers question why chromatin opening imposes such large delay and whether this reflects reporter complexity rather than endogenous gene behavior, requesting validation with in situ hybridization.

Both evaluate Random Telegraph model (C46, C47, C56). LLM finds model successfully fits data with consistent parameters. Peer reviewers identify confusion in mathematical formulation, questioning whether x-axis is time, whether a and b are rates vs times, and requesting clarification of formulas and terminology.

Both address frequency modulation as core finding (C2, C27, C60, C72). LLM finds converging evidence strongly supports dose-dependent frequency with invariant duration. Peer reviewers acknowledge technical novelty but question conceptual novelty, stating findings 'mostly confirmed previous observations' about digital on-off states, requesting clarification of novelty beyond prior work.

Both express uncertainty about 'one dose yields one cycle' claim (C69, C70, C75). LLM notes 70% show single bursts but 30% show no burst or multiple bursts. Peer reviewers request statistical analysis of probabilities for single vs multiple cycles and comparison of on-periods to steady-state dosing, indicating incomplete evidence.

Both note unresolved mechanistic questions about timing (C90, C91, C94). LLM identifies discrepancy between FRAP-measured SR dwell times and burst durations, noting speculative hypotheses lack direct evidence. Peer reviewers question the biological basis of the long delay and whether it reflects reporter complexity.

Partial overlap on clonal variation (C57, C58, C84). LLM finds evidence for insertion site-dependent effects convincing. Peer reviewers question whether analyses were performed per clone and note unclear data presentation, indicating uncertainty about proper validation across cell lines.

Both express concerns about photoactivation experiments (C66, C71). LLM notes modest sample size and unexplained variability. Peer reviewers raise concerns about cell health (nuclear blebbing, apoptosis indicators) and potential DNA damage from UV exposure, requesting γ-H2A.X labeling controls to rule out artifacts.

Minimal overlap on population-level dose response (C3, C73). LLM finds FISH data showing heterogeneous single-cell distributions aggregating to smooth Hill functions convincing. Peer reviewers question conceptual novelty of digital-to-analog findings relative to prior work.

Minimal overlap on reporter system (C35). LLM finds dual-modality system well-designed and thoroughly documented. Peer reviewers question whether single transcription site per cell is confirmed and whether it's stably maintained through generations, indicating uncertainty about single-copy validation.

LLM evaluates FISH dose-response data (C43-C45, C52-C55) showing heterogeneous single-cell distributions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about mRNA distribution heterogeneity and Hill function parameters.

LLM evaluates chromatin's role in burst timing (C95-C101) based on cited literature and histone turnover timescales. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these claims about chromatin regulation mechanisms.

LLM evaluates comprehensive reporter system design (C24-C38, C104-C110) including MS2/FISH integration, lentiviral approach, and clonal selection. Peer reviewers address only single aspects (C35) rather than comprehensive system validation.
